images.filename: I was surprised to see no lightning conductor above the dome (38221673934).jpg
images.caption: Our guide pointed out to a large bronze bell in a belfry right atop the tall central arch of the Hall Bazaar side entrance to the Town Hall. Ah, so there is a bell in there! Thanks to the sheer height of the belfry, it's very easy to miss the belfry altogether, let alone the bell inside it. The bell is defunct- no one rings it any more now. And considering the height of the dome, I was surprised to see no lightning conductor atop it. Blind faith in god perhaps. I joked light heartedly. My companions did not react at all, probably taking the remark to be not funny enough or being blasphemous! (Amritsar, Punjab, northern India, Nov. 2017)

images.filename: Imposing entrance arch to the Town Hall- Partition Museum in Amritsar (24074291387).jpg
images.caption: It's a brand new, and breakkie done, the order of business for this morning is a heritage walk into the congested old town district of Amritsar. Our guide will meet us near the Amritsar Town Hall, of which this is one of the portals. This long shot taken by my brother shows my sister and I walking under the portals, accompanied by our Sikh guide. My brother joined us soon after taking this picture. The Amritsar Town Hall was built by the British in 1866, and was the then centre of the Amritsar's local administration. (Amritsar, Punjab, northern India, Nov. 2017)

images.filename: Overall view of the Town Hall- Partition Museum (38938332321).jpg
images.caption: An overall view of the Amritsar Town Hall from its large forecourt. The buses are probably for Government officials. I had taken the previous picture of the Hall Bazaar gate through that large arch you see up ahead. (though not from this far- we were closer then). The Amritsar Town Hall now houses the totally absorbing and poignant Partition Museum- we will talk about that later in this album. (see subsequent pictures) (Amritsar, Punjab, northern India, Nov. 2017)
